body:
Router now defaults routed geolocation headers to removal and requires explicit per-request consent before forwarding supported location metadata. It also hardens the existing client privacy defaults and documents the limits of those controls. This draft remains unfinished: universal tool/account privacy and the complete JavaScript-first parity requirements have not been verified.

Fixes #784

## Behavior and reproduction

Before this change, clients could forward geolocation and ingress network metadata without an explicit location-sharing request. The Router request path now parses and validates the consent control, strips it before upstream forwarding, rejects ambiguous values, and removes location and ingress network headers by default. The explicit location opt-in does not authorize forwarding ingress identity headers. Provider-specific, retry, streaming, management, and persisted-policy routes retain regression coverage. Client configuration and documentation distinguish routed request controls from direct vendor traffic, account settings, source-IP visibility, OAuth, MCP, telemetry and retention.

This does not establish a universal vendor/account geolocation guarantee. The remaining acceptance inventory and investigation are in [the case study](docs/case-studies/issue-784/README.md). No required sub-issues were identified. No existing feature was intentionally removed.

## Current coordinated repair batch

Previous published head `93995ee40be4b570becbe0b788dba58f5bd0ea6f` was tested as merge `b0ea6ee80521788e7cba7f47488034c40f5a85e4`. [Run 42879038865](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/actions/runs/42879038865) finished at 2026-11-10 20:12:00 UTC: 17 failed, 11 successful, 6 cancelled and 25 skipped jobs. All three applicable workflows are terminal. All 23 nonpassing logs and all 26 complete artifacts were read and retained before publishing this coordinated batch. No run was cancelled. The [complete terminal review](docs/case-studies/issue-784/ci-939-terminal-20261110.md) records every failure, exact source/deadline errors and whole-byte custody.

The coordinated batch through `82bff66b3eaec603e296f1d888fe909dad4743c8`:

- Regenerates and independently installs the complete current selected-Git compiler registration, preserving original sources, full 1934-file census and historical registry. Both complete receiving files pass all 16 cases on Node and Bun within unchanged deadlines. [Registration evidence](docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-939-registration.md).
- Isolates Node compiler process trees using sixteen exhaustive whole-file bins and one worker per runner. Both complete workflow/runner files pass all 45 controls. Every current/future file, original deadline, independent audit, source census, freshness command and same-SHA gate remains mandatory. Bun retains eight bins. [Source equations and validation](docs/case-studies/issue-784/isolated-node-translation-shards.md).
- Fully inspects all 2873 nested canonical outputs (320408059 original bytes) and current physical input pins. Only inventory differs among outputs, but three repaired compiler inputs have changed. The old artifact is not installed or treated as current generation.
- Retains complete native-erasure and TAR-loop experiments without applying them. The whole 14-function base64 translation is slower with the proposed TAR loop, so production inputs were restored exactly.
- Preserves complete terminal evidence in durable custody. Only identified inactive local copies already published at immutable Git blobs are retired after complete byte verification, with reclaimed-space receipts.

Earlier changes retain the actual producer's canonical output refresh, complete source-history repairs, actual ordinary reverse regeneration and all original regression files. Current canonical CI reports 165 executable top-level production functions, 391 constants and 179 types; 12426 carried items and partial projects remain. Neither metadata counts nor source preservation establish complete parity or a newly executable function gain for this batch.

## Validation and limitations

Lockfile-installed TypeScript is **5.9.3**, Node **20.20.2**, local Bun **1.4.4**; CI pins Bun 1.4.3. Strictness, complete original test files, case/child/job deadlines and raw compiler source bounds remain unchanged.

- Current registration: all 16 original cases pass in each engine, with complete independent source/deadline evidence.
- Current workflow/runner: 45 cases pass, no failures, cancellations or skips; actual workflow source producer `--check` passes with complete serialized/reparsed CST equations and inverses.
- Complete runtime-import file with one Node worker: seven assertions pass, but the full original/current build comparison takes **190815.839221/60000 ms**. The independent auditor correctly exits 1. This does not qualify the deadline or prove a contention improvement.
- Latest whole local gate at `bcf84c063f06754ba48aa7d2c4c23e48bfdbd5ce`: lint, both 259-case native runtime suites, deadline controls, declarations, native freshness and strict 167-file native TypeScript pass. The full nine-case native TypeScript file completes but its original regeneration case takes **78857.500265/60000 ms**, failing its independent deadline audit.
- That gate is then memory-interrupted in parity acceptance after 104 assertions, at **2867023872 bytes** in this **3135369216-byte** container. Nine later TypeScript commands, strict parity and forward/reverse stages remain unrun for that attempt. [Complete evidence](docs/case-studies/issue-784/current-complete-gates-20261110.md). No subsequent whole-gate success is claimed.

**Still required:** fresh same-SHA green CI and complete local gate; genuine current canonical/owned/profile generation and strict compilation; owned reverse freshness; strict parity and every original case/child/job deadline; raw private compiler source bound; universal tool/account privacy acceptance. Finished CI still reports 441 draft parity gaps and one validation error, missing owned matrix input, stale inventory, original long-running compiler cases and job cancellations. Pre-existing main failures remain mandatory. No missing secret or human access requirement was identified; no credential skip or manual-action workaround was introduced. Rust remains gated until every JavaScript stage passes for the same SHA. No Rust tool runs locally.

Main `eb2dad1c0a18394dc1aad46413e11401e74eb502` was freshly fetched and is already an ancestor. The issue has no comments or required sub-issues. All seven PR conversation comments, zero inline comments and zero reviews were refreshed and read. GitHub's PR diff endpoint refuses this change set because it exceeds 300 files; local diffs are used for review. The PR remains draft and unmerged. This feedback checkpoint establishes no completion or release readiness.
title: Default routed geolocation sharing to explicit per-request consent
